coeffDescription.message: Estimate tokens per character (CJK/Kana/Hangul) or per word (Cyrillic/Arabic/Latin). Higher = more tokens for that script.

estimationGuideText.message: Headroom estimates token counts from the conversation text using per-script coefficients — it never trusts the platform's own count. CJK ideographs, Japanese kana, and Korean Hangul are counted per character. Cyrillic, Arabic, and Latin (and anything else) are counted per whitespace-separated word. Each script has a coefficient that represents the average tokens per counting unit for that model's tokenizer, calibrated by observing real tokenizer output. You can adjust these coefficients per platform in the Advanced settings above. Web-search results and tool-call text are counted into the round's total the same way, shown in the Search/Tool column of the round table.

platformRefNoteDeepseek.message: Measured against the open DeepSeek-V4 tokenizer (exact). Chinese is cheap: ~0.6 tok/ch; Cyrillic/Arabic ~2.1 tok/wd.

platformRefNoteChatgpt.message: Measured offline with tiktoken o200k_base (exact — GPT-5.6 keeps the same tokenizer, confirmed 2026-08). CJK ~0.8 tok/ch; Latin ~1.3 tok/wd.

platformRefNoteGemini.message: Tokenizer not public; measured via Gemma 4 — Google's open family, 262K SentencePiece in the same lineage; 3.6 Flash's tokenizer unconfirmed unchanged. CJK ~0.7 tok/ch.

platformRefNoteKimi.message: Measured against the open Kimi K3 tiktoken vocab (exact). Chinese ~0.6 tok/ch; Cyrillic/Arabic words are costly (~2.8 tok/wd).

platformRefNoteQwen.message: Measured against the open Qwen tokenizer (exact — Qwen3.8-Max open weights ship the same vocab as 3.6). CJK ~0.6 tok/ch.

platformRefNoteQianwen.message: Same tokenizer family as Qwen — shares the same measured coefficients.

platformRefNoteDoubao.message: Closed tokenizer; measured via ByteDance's open Seed-OSS-36B (still the latest open Seed model, 2026-08) as proxy. Tune if the gauge drifts — kana is the least reliable value.
